messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: SEV-2 - service 'inference-frontend' triggered (PD-84731). Automatic escalation in 5m if unacked. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-84731

emma: taking this — I’m oncall. seeing increased 5xx on /v1/generate, spike at 3:14 UTC.

raj: acked and joining. I see a big tail latency on kvcache lookups (redis misses up ~10x). Could be key eviction.

oliver: jumping in. checking autoscaler and node health. Any customer-facing errors reported?

emma: customers getting 502/504. Some retries from SDKs causing burst. Impact: partial for hosted-api, embeddings & chat endpoints degraded.

raj: running quick heatmap: 
```
# redis info keyspace
used_memory_human: 12.3G
maxmemory_policy: volatile-lru
evicted_keys: 5234
instantaneous_ops_per_sec: 1200
```
Looks like eviction pressure. Eviction correlates with recent rollout of batching change.

oliver: which rollout? eng-runtime or routing?

emma: eng-runtime pushed 2026-03-13 02:20 (batching heuristics tweak). Could cause larger prefixes flush.

raj: quick mitigation: set redis maxmemory-policy to noeviction for hot-keys? risky. Alternative: increase redis nodes and restore cache warmers.

oliver: we should enable PD failover route to dedicated pool for critical customers while we mitigate. That buys time.

emma: taking ownership of customer comms. I’ll post status on status.redwood.ai and add affected customers list.

sara: I can flip routing to the smaller, lower-latency model variant (model-v1-lite) as a controlled fallback for non-enterprise customers. Rollback path ready. :+1:

raj: prepping commands — scaling redis cluster + bumping ensure CPU headroom. Running: 
```
kubectl -n infra scale statefulset/redis-cluster --replicas=5
redis-cli -h redis-proxy INFO | grep keyspace
```

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-13T02:18:54 (eng-runtime) rollback candidate found: artifact a1b2c3. /deploy rollback ready.

oliver: ok plan: 1) route non-enterprise to model-v1-lite (sara) 2) scale redis (raj) 3) if tail persists, rollback eng-runtime batching tweak (deploy-bot/emma) 4) monitor 10m and escalate if error rate not back to baseline.

emma: executing customer routing change now: routing rule 45 -> model-v1-lite for tier != enterprise.

sara: done, propagation taking ~30s. latency for routed traffic down on initial checks.

raj: redis cluster scaled to 5 replicas, rebalancing keys. eviction rate dropping.

emma: PD status update: acknowledged by emma & raj. owner: emma. Current impact: degraded (partial). ETA for initial mitigation: 12 minutes.

oliver: monitoring dashboards: 5xx rate down ~40% since reroute. KV miss rate down 60% after replicas. Good sign.

emma: customer comms posted: "We are investigating elevated errors for text generation. Temporary fallback to alternative model applied for most customers. We will update in 15 minutes."

raj: small regression observed in tail latency for embeddings pipeline. If that persists after cache stabilizes, we’ll consider rollback.

emma: decision checkpoint in 10m. Please ping here with health metrics.

sara: ping: embeddings tail 95p still ~1.8s (was 1.1s). Not ideal but functional.

oliver: recommend holding rollback for now — reroute + scale seems to be improving user-visible errors. Rolling back risks reintroducing eviction.

emma: agreed. keeping the change paused. If stable in 15m, we’ll move to postmortem & follow-up.

raj: creating incident ticket PD-84731 -> JIRA INF-5923 and attaching initial findings.

incident-bot: PD-84731: acknowledged by emma, raj. Escalation timer cancelled.

emma: closing loop: owner emma will file postmortem draft, include timeline, root-cause hypothesis (batching heuristic + cache eviction), and remediation (warmers, prefilling, safer rollout gating). Marking incident as mitigated for now.

oliver: thanks team — good coordination.

sara: adding follow-up action: add canary for batching changes to avoid global key eviction.

emma: end of thread — moving to incident postmortem channel for the write-up. :white_check_mark:
